extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors and managers, media researchers, and interested members of the public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for producing or assessing constructive (solutions-focused) journalism — an approach that supplements traditional news reporting with solution-focused, contextual, and future-oriented perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate problems alongside responses and solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigates problems alongside responses and solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive journalism seeks to supplement traditional reporting by adding coverage of how individuals, institutions, and communities address problems — not by avoiding the problem but by investigating both the problem and existing or emergent responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context, nuance and multiple stakeholder perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides context, nuance and multiple stakeholder perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should broaden reporting through contextualization and inclusion of diverse stakeholders to give a fuller and more accurate portrayal of societal conditions rather than simplistic or decontextualized problem framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate forward-looking and explanatory questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporates forward-looking and explanatory questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use questions and framing that explore implications, possible futures, mechanisms, and explanations (for example, ‘‘what happens next?’’, ‘‘how did this come about?’’) to move beyond immediate events toward longer-term understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight progress, agency and evidence-backed initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlights progress, agency and evidence-backed initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize where there is measurable progress, the agency of individuals/communities, and initiatives that are supported by evidence — without overstating results or certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism, distortion, and binary framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoids sensationalism, distortion, and binary framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive journalism explicitly rejects sensationalist language and simplistic binaries; reporting should resist distortion and seek nuance instead of polarizing or hyperbolic presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain core journalistic values (accuracy, independence, verification, scrutiny)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retains traditional journalistic values such as accuracy and independence, verification, and scrutiny while broadening reporting to include responses and possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive approaches must not replace verification or critical scrutiny — accuracy and editorial independence remain essential. Solutions/positive angles must be evidence-based and subject to the same fact-checking and critical analysis as other reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions (six-element constructive model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions — one of the six core elements of constructive journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of a widely cited model (solutions, future orientation, context, inclusivity, empowerment, co-creation). Emphasize concrete responses and interventions related to the problem under coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future orientation (six-element constructive model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Future orientation — one of the six core elements of constructive journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should explicitly consider future scenarios, trajectories, and long-term implications rather than focusing solely on immediate events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context (six-element constructive model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Context — one of the six core elements of constructive journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide background, systemic factors, historical perspective and data that explain why a problem exists and how responses fit within larger systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity (six-element constructive model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusivity — one of the six core elements of constructive journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure diverse voices and stakeholders are included, particularly those affected by the issue; avoid excluding or marginalizing perspectives that are relevant to understanding solutions and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empowerment (six-element constructive model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Empowerment — one of the six core elements of constructive journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to increase audience agency, perceived efficacy or capacity to engage with issues, without providing prescriptive advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-creation (six-element constructive model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-creation — one of the six core elements of constructive journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage audiences, communities, or stakeholders in the production process (participatory formats) so reporting benefits from local knowledge and shared ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive interviewing (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive interviewing using past- and future-oriented questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview techniques should include both reflective (past) and anticipatory (future) questioning to surface how people understand problems and envision or enact responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions-focused research frameworks alongside problem investigation (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions-focused research frameworks alongside problem investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt research methods that actively look for and evaluate responses and solutions in addition to documenting problems; combine investigative rigor with solution assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-creation and participatory journalism (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-creation and participatory journalism (for example, Room of Solutions formats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use participatory formats that involve citizens or affected communities in identifying problems and shaping or testing solutions; examples include Room of Solutions and citizen dialogue formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual and data-informed storytelling (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual and data-informed storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data, long-form context, and explanatory storytelling to situate problems and solutions within systems and trends rather than presenting isolated anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario and foresight questioning (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenario and foresight questions about long-term developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate scenario thinking and foresight questions to explore plausible futures, trade-offs and long-term consequences of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen dialogue formats (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizen dialogue formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate dialogues between citizens, experts, and policymakers as part of reporting to surface practical insights and community-led responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longitudinal solution tracking (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Longitudinal “solution tracking” in communities and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow initiatives and interventions over time to assess effectiveness, unintended consequences, and scalability rather than reporting a one-off outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim: counteract news fatigue, news avoidance and negativity bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim is to counteract news fatigue and news avoidance, negativity bias and disengagement by adding nuance, evidence-based responses, and forward-looking angles to stories about societal challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive journalism is explicitly positioned as a response to audience disengagement and negativity bias; success criteria include improved engagement, comprehension, perceived relevance, and trust where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid normative or advocacy drift (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk of normative or advocacy drift if 'solutions' are framed uncritically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial distance and rigorous evaluation of solutions; avoid adopting or promoting particular interventions without independent verification and transparent evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid blurring journalism and strategic communication (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible blurring of boundaries between journalism and strategic communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious that participatory/co-created formats and engagement with solution actors do not convert reporting into advocacy or PR; preserve independence and critical oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource and time constraints in newsrooms (practical limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource and time constraints in newsrooms, especially for daily hard news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive methods often require more time, research and follow-up than routine breaking-news coverage; plan resources and workflows accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges adapting constructive methods to breaking news (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges in adapting constructive methods to fast-paced breaking news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some constructive approaches (longitudinal tracking, deep context) are difficult to apply in immediate, rapidly evolving stories; use selective integration and maintain standards of verification under time pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overstating effectiveness or certainty of interventions (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concern that solutions narratives may overstate effectiveness or certainty of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should explicitly communicate limits of evidence, uncertainties and potential negative consequences; avoid definitive claims about success without robust supporting data.
